messages.subject: Re: Fixing Legend in Animations
parts:
See inline.

On 10/2/2012 4:45 AM, Isaiah wrote:
> Hi, I am plotting the positions of vehicles, called "names", as the travel
> on a journey. I make the plots using ggplot, then join then in an
> animation.
>
> At any time, a vehicle may enter or leave the viewing area. When this
> happens, the legend changes to reflect the entry or exit. This is
> distracting. Is there some way to fix the legend listing, so it includes
> all vehicles at all times, not just those in a particular plot?
>
> Also, the vehicle names are of different lengths. As vehicles enter or
> exit, the width of the legend changes with the length of the longest name.
> Is there some way to fix the legend with? This is key for the animation to
> work, as the plot size changes as the legend size changes. I've tried
> adding trailing blanks, but these seem to be stripped. I'm now adding
> trailing "_" which works, but is a little ugly.
>
> Below are the key parts of the script:

Since you only include the "key parts", the script is not reproducible,
so it is hard to be sure what the problem is.

> #pad out names so legend width doesn't change
>
> longest.name<-max(nchar(as.character(Data.Frame$NAME)))
>
> Data.Frame$NAME
> <-as.factor(str_pad(as.character(Data.Frame$NAME),longest.name,side="right",
> pad = "_"))
>
>
>
> #loop through times
>
> i<-1
>
> Step<-10
>
> while (i <= time.events){
>
> x<-subset(Data.Frame, DATETIME==time[i])
>
> filename <- paste("file",i,".png", sep="")
>
> p<-ggplot()+geom_point(data=x, aes(xcoord, ycoord, colour=NAME), size=5)

I thinking adding

+ scale_colour_discrete(drop=FALSE)

will work. Then all the levels of name/colour will show up in the legend
all the time, so then padding shouldn't be a necessity either.

> png(file=filename, width = 1024, height = 768)
>
> print(p)
>
> dev.off()
>
> print(i)
>
> i<-i+Step
>
> }
>
> # Do animation
>
> files = sprintf('file%d.png', seq(from=1, to=time.events, by=Step))
>
> im.convert(files, output = 'View.gif')
>
> (R beginner, btw).
>
